correctness.rationale: The stationary density is a positive unit-trace Poisson-age integral and the stationary resolvent is invertible for r>0. Direct 9x9 elimination yields the stated population formulas and determinant, with exact symbolic reconstruction and 56 independent complex matrix solves. The maximizing polynomial has exactly one positive root for every nonzero flux by Descartes rule and endpoints. The positive flux envelope identity and small-flux expansion prove the unique joint optimum and noncommuting limit. Numerical checks corroborate but are not used as an infinite proof.

value.rationale: Direction-selective stationary quantum-site sampling is a natural observable in a minimal loop with gauge flux. The theorem finds a complete rate/flux optimum and a finite optimal detection contrast in the vanishing-flux limit, despite identically zero contrast at zero flux; this noncommuting control limit is not exposed by general renewal formulas or numerical scans. It is relevant to calibrating competing coherent splitting and reset timescales, without implying experimental noise robustness.
